title: Why the Moon, Not the Sun, Dominates Tides

segments.text: The Sun is 20 million times heavier, but it sits 400 times farther away.
Tidal force drops with the cube of distance.
The Moon’s proximity makes its gradient steeper.
The Moon’s pull changes rapidly across Earth, while the Sun’s pull is almost flat.
That steep slope creates a larger bulge.
The lunar tide is twice the solar tide.
The Sun’s tide is only 45 percent of the Moon’s.

question: Where do you notice the biggest tide change on your coast?
